issues.description: Method Course.getAverageRating() has different return types across artifacts. The problem statement (problem_statement.md) explicitly requires getAverageRating() to return a Double. The template implementation (Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift in the template repository) declares the method signature as `func getAverageRating() -> Double`. The solution implementation (Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift in the solution repository) declares the method signature as `func getAverageRating() -> Float`. This inconsistency can confuse students about the expected return type and may cause compilation or test mismatches when students follow the problem statement/template but compare against the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across all artifacts. Preferably change the solution implementation to return Double to match the problem statement and template: update the signature in Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift (solution) to `func getAverageRating() -> Double` and perform calculations using Double (e.g., cast sums and counts to Double before dividing). Alternatively, if Float is preferred, update the problem statement and the template to require Float — but ensure all three artifacts (problem statement, template, solution) use the same return type.
